decisions.context: Problem in their words is an ASSUMPTION. Before post 1, has any head of credit, lending-ops lead or lender CTO actually said they distrust AI underwriting because they can't trace the figures? Needs interviews (e.g. 5 people from the NACFB list), not memory.
options: Yes: 3 or more conversations, with their wording written down
No: it comes from the research doc and the playbook

decisions.context: Is the segment on LinkedIn at all? Evidence task 1 (how many of the 20 outreach targets posted or commented in the last 30 days) hasn't been run. If 3 or fewer, the channel is wrong whatever the algorithm does.

The 'baseline zero' leaves out the starting audience. The 'interest graph' still needs some first readers in the segment. Export your LinkedIn connections and count those whose title or company matches the 'who' (credit, lending ops, CTO at UK SME lenders or brokers).

Attribution and readability: the playbook's week-3 outreach to 10 brokers and lenders falls inside the same 6 weeks, so outreach calls will be counted as post-driven. 'Target segment' has no named list, and LinkedIn's free tier doesn't show reliable job titles for profile viewers. How will the tally separate the two?
options: Tag every DM and call by source (post / outreach / other) and count only post-sourced ones against the bet
Push the outreach back to week 7 so the window only measures posts
Fix a named list of about 40 target accounts up front and count only contacts from it

decisions.context: Credibility: the 7 Nov panel failed v0.1 (C1 blocker: invented `£48k`/`£1.2m` pass the guard; C3: sign error flips the policy). The bet asks for an outside analyst to run a statement through the agent in this window. What ships before the first post on 9 Nov?
options: C1–C6 fixed and panel run 02 passes before post 1; start date moves if needed
Post now, but lead with the panel failure as the build story and hold the 'run your statement' ask until it passes
Post as planned on the current v0.1

decisions.context: Buying path: today they hire agencies or vendors they already know, which is tolerable partly because those firms already passed vendor and outsourcing due diligence. Would a UK SME lender take on an individual freelancer outside that? Ask 3 heads of credit how they found and onboarded their last outside tech supplier.
options: Directly, through a referral or LinkedIn contact, with light onboarding
Only through an approved vendor or consultancy, so partnering or subcontracting is the real route
Only for paid advisory or assessment work, not production systems

decisions.context: Gate: evidence task 2 (contract social-media and IP clauses) is unresolved, and the bet's own kill criterion depends on it. A clause on outside work, conflict of interest or competing with the employer could stop public work on a lending product, even with no employer named.
options: Checked: posting and building the product are allowed
Checked: needs employer approval or a disclosure first
Checked: blocks it, so the plan has to change
